newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FORECAST - Taiwan April M2 seen up 10.12 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Taiwan April M2 seen up 10.12 pct yr/yr.

text.p: A Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists on Thursday projected an average 10.12 percent year-on-year rise in April for M2, the island's broadest money supply figure.
The figure was to be issued by the central bank after 0300 GMT on May 24.
M2 grew a year-on-year 9.90 percent in March.
The following table gives institutions' forecasts for Taiwan's annual M2 growth in April in percent:
Institution M2 growth
Core Pacific Securities 10.4
Grand Cathay Securities 10.2
HSBC James Capel 9.8
National Securities 9.7
Nomura Securities 10.5
Average 10.12
Economists said they expected April M2 growth to fall into the central bank's target zone of 9-14 percent growth for the fourth straight month.

After more than a year below the target zone, M2 began falling with the zone in January -- after the central bank slightly broadened its M2 definition. Economists estimate the revision added some one to 1.5 percentage points to M2 growth.
Economists noted that demand for money was slowly increasing due to a recovering domestic economy.
"Money demand has kept on rising due to the domestic recovery, and the central bank apparently has not tightened liquidity," said Nomura Securities economist Amy Huang.

They said bank financing to individuals had increased due to the stock market's first-quarter surge, but banks' corporate financing did not grow significantly due to firms' shift to direct self-financing to raise money for investments.
"M2 growth will not be strong as corporations have increased their direct financing, which is not reflected in M2," said Grand Cathay Securities vice-president Terry Chen.
In recent quarters, Taiwan companies have often sought to raise funds through direct financing, chiefly issuance of local corporate bonds and convertible bonds and global depositary receipts abroad.
The Taiwan share index once had risen some 25 percent in 1997 alone as of late April, although May has seen a modest correction.
Until January, the central bank's money supply categories were defined as follows:
--M1A: cash, checking accounts and passbook deposits
--M1B: M1A plus savings accounts
--M2: M1B plus quasi-money.

In the revision, the bank said it would maintain its M1A and M1B definition unchanged, while M2 now would include M1B plus time deposits, foreign currency deposits, postal funds, repurchase agreement trade outstanding and foreigners' Taiwan dollar holdings.

The new M2 definition uses post offices' total deposits instead of their redeposits in banks, adds repurchase agreement trade outstanding and foreigners' Taiwan dollar holdings, and deletes the net value of financial bonds, savings bonds and treasury bills and foreign-currency trust funds.
-- Taipei Newsroom (2-5080815)
